class.name: PhysXDebrisSurge3D
class.brief_description: Boulders and mud spray at the front of a post-fire debris flow.
class.description: Listens for the weather's [code]debris_flow[/code] events on [WorldGround] (fired by [code]WeatherRunoff3D[/code] when a storm on a burnt basin passes its debris-flow threshold) and draws what rides the flow's front. The mud body itself belongs to the ground ([code]GroundDebrisFlow3D[/code]). Each event runs as a train of up to [member surge_count_max] surges, [member surge_interval] apart, the first the biggest (post-fire debris flows arrive in surges: Kean et al. 2011). A surge's front runs down the event's channel path at Rickenmann's (1999) speed v = 2.1 Q^(1/3) S^(1/3), with peak discharge Q = 0.1 V^(5/6) for its volume. It is as deep as Q = v w h gives, and it stops where the slope falls below [member stop_slope], on its fan. Where [member front_source] reports a front for the event, the surge follows that instead. Boulders and cobbles of the coarse fraction (sizes from a power law up to [member max_boulder], no bigger than the flow is deep) ride as rigid bodies. The flow's drag carries them and the dense slurry buoys them. The flow behind the snout outruns the front, so they gather at the snout (Iverson 1997) and come to rest in its lobe when it stops. Mud spray flies up at the front.

method.name: clear
method.description: Removes every surge, boulder and drop.

method.name: get_active_surges
method.description: Surges whose fronts are running now.

method.name: get_front_depth
method.description: A surge's flow depth at its front, in metres.

method.name: get_front_position
method.description: Where a surge's front is, on its path.

method.name: get_front_speed
method.description: A surge's front speed in m/s.

method.name: get_peak_discharge
method.description: Rickenmann's peak discharge (m³/s) for a debris flow of [param volume] m³.

method.name: start
method.description: Starts the surges of one debris-flow event, a dictionary with the keys of the weather's [code]debris_flow[/code] event: [code]id[/code], [code]volume[/code] (m³), [code]path[/code] (a [PackedVector3Array] from the outlet downhill, on the ground) and [code]widths[/code] (channel widths in metres per path point). It is called for every event the weather fires while [member listen] is on.

members.member: A node with [code]get_debris_front(event_id)[/code] returning the mud body's front ([code]position[/code], [code]path_index[/code], [code]depth[/code], [code]speed[/code], [code]width[/code], [code]done[/code]), such as the ground's [code]GroundDebrisFlow3D[/code]. Empty, or with no front for an event, the surge runs its own front.
If [code]true[/code], starts surges for the weather's debris-flow events.
The biggest boulder across, in metres.
Colour of the spray (dark with ash after a fire).
Density of the flowing mud, kg/m³; it buoys the boulders.
How much mud spray the fronts throw; 0 for none.
The slope (rise over run) below which a front slows to a stop.
The most surges in one event (one per 400 m³).
Seconds between surges, give or take 30%.
